small_guidance:
- The conv kernel is doing C_in=64 × KH×KW=9 = 576 scalar loads of x and w per output element with no register reuse across output channels — switch to autotune over BLOCK_HW ∈ {64,128,256}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3} and try processing multiple C_out per program (BLOCK_C tile) so the input gather is amortized across output channels.
- Eliminate the intermediate write by fusing the avgpool into conv_tanh_sub: one program produces a POOL×POOL tile of conv outputs, applies tanh/sub, sums and divides — saves an N*C_out*H_out*W_out global write+read.
- Pre-cast and store weight in a layout (C_out, KH*KW, C_in) and load a full C_in vector via tl.dot against an x tile, turning the inner triple loop into a small GEMM.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style implicit GEMM: program tiles over (N, output-spatial tile of pooled grid, BLOCK_OC), accumulator shape [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_HW] computed via tl.dot over a K-loop of size C_in*KH*KW with BLOCK_K=32 or 64. This is the standard high-throughput conv pattern and will give 10-50× over the current naive direct conv.
- Fuse the entire pipeline (conv + sub1 + tanh + sub2 + avgpool) in a single kernel: each program owns one pooled output tile, computes the POOL×POOL conv outputs in registers from the GEMM accumulator, applies the elementwise epilogue, reduces, and writes the pooled result — no intermediate tensor.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) layout for x and (KH*KW*C_in, C_out) for w so the GEMM-K dimension is contiguous and loads coalesce; do the layout transform once on the weight in __init__ (constant) and on x at forward entry.
